recipes.title: Makki di Roti
recipes.description: Punjabi cornmeal flatbread patted out by hand and cooked on a tava, the classic partner for sarson da saag.

steps.instructionText: Heap the cornmeal in a wide tray (praat), make a well in the centre and pour in a little of the lukewarm water.
Mix into a dough, adding water a little at a time so it stays moist but not sticky. Sprinkle in more cornmeal if it gets sticky.
Add the butter and give the dough a final knead.
Roll a hand-sized portion into a ball, then flatten it between wet palms, turning it as you go so it thins evenly.
Press any cracks at the edges back together. Wet your fingers to help spread it into a round about the size of a small plate.
Place the roti on a preheated iron tava and leave it until it can be moved. Press any moist-looking areas with a dry cloth.
Turn it over and cook the other side until no moist areas remain; a few slightly charred spots are normal.
Serve hot with sarson da saag and lassi.

recipes.title: Malai Mix Veg
recipes.description: Mixed vegetables and paneer in a creamy tomato-cashew gravy, a rich side for naan or roti.

ingredients.name: coloured capsicums (1 each orange, yellow and red)

steps.instructionText: Cut the green capsicums and coloured capsicums into 1 cm pieces.
Sauté the paneer cubes until golden brown and set aside.
Soak most of the cashew nuts in warm water, keeping a few for garnish.
Grind the tomatoes and soaked cashew nuts into a fine paste and set aside.
Sauté the capsicums, carrot, peas, green chillies and dried parsley in the butter until the vegetables are cooked.
Add the tomato paste to the vegetables and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the garam masala, red chilli powder, salt and turmeric to taste and simmer for 2 minutes.
Add the whipping cream and sour cream and cook until the cream thickens.
Add the fried paneer and mix well.
Garnish with the coriander leaves and remaining cashew nuts, and serve hot with naan or roti.

recipes.title: Matar Paneer
recipes.description: Fried paneer cubes and green peas in a spiced onion-tomato gravy, finished with a chilli tadka.

ingredients.name: green chillies, seeded and finely chopped

steps.instructionText: Heat some of the oil in a deep pan. Fry the paneer cubes on all sides over medium-low heat until golden brown, then drain on paper towels.
Pour off the excess oil from the same pan. Add the ginger-garlic paste and onions and cook, stirring, until the onions are translucent.
Add the puréed tomatoes and cook over medium heat until their liquid has dried up. Turn off the heat and let it cool.
Blend the onion-tomato mixture with the green chillies until smooth.
Heat a little more oil in the pan and fry the cumin seeds until they crackle.
Add the turmeric powder, 1/2 tsp of the red chilli powder, the coriander powder and garam masala. Mix well over low heat.
Add the blended purée and mix well over medium heat. Season with the salt and mix in the peas.
Add the water, cover and cook until the peas are fully cooked.
Uncover, add the fried paneer and mix well, adding more water if needed.
For the tadka, heat 1 tsp oil in a small pan, add the remaining red chilli powder and mix. Turn off the heat.
Pour the tadka over the matar paneer, garnish with the coriander leaves and serve.

recipes.title: Murgh Musallam
recipes.description: Marinated chicken simmered with a freshly ground Mughlai spice blend, onion paste and almond-cashew paste.

steps.instructionText: Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces and wash well.
Mix the chicken with 1 tbsp of the ginger-garlic paste, the lemon juice, 2 tsp red chilli powder, black pepper powder, turmeric powder and 1/2 tsp salt. Marinate for 1 to 4 hours.
For the spice blend, dry roast the coriander seeds, cumin seeds, whole spices (5 cm cinnamon, 2 green and 1 black cardamom, 4 cloves, 1 mace) and nutmeg until light brown and aromatic.
Let the spices cool, then grind them to a coarse powder.
Soak the almonds and cashews in water for 10-15 minutes. Peel the almonds and grind both to a smooth paste with 1-2 tbsp water.
Heat 2-3 tsp of the oil or ghee and sauté the onions until golden brown. Cool and grind to a paste, adding as little water as possible.
Heat the remaining oil or ghee, add the onion paste, green chillies and remaining ginger-garlic paste, and sauté until the oil separates.
Add the marinated chicken and mix well. Cover and cook over medium-low heat for 5-6 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Mix in the remaining red chilli powder, the ground spice blend and the tomato. Cover and cook, stirring occasionally, until oil floats on top.
Add the water and cook over medium heat for 3-4 minutes.
Mix in the nut paste, mint leaves and salt to taste. Cook until the gravy thickens and oil floats on top.
Remove from the heat and stir in the coriander leaves.

recipes.title: Chicken Korma
recipes.description: Mild, creamy chicken curry with whole spices, coconut cream and saffron, topped with fried onions.

ingredients.name: chicken, skinned and cut into medium pieces

steps.instructionText: Mix the chicken with the ginger paste, garlic paste, coriander powder, cumin powder, nutmeg powder and Greek yogurt. Cover and marinate in the fridge for 1-3 hours.
Fry the onions in the ghee until they start to brown but are still soft, not crisp. Lift them out with a slotted spoon and set aside.
Add the marinated chicken to the hot ghee and cook over medium heat.
Dry toast the cardamom pods, cloves and cinnamon stick in a hot frying pan for 1 minute until aromatic.
Add the toasted spices and black pepper to the chicken. Cover and cook, stirring occasionally.
When water starts to separate from the chicken, add the coconut cream, salt and sugar. Add a little boiling water if it dries out before the chicken is cooked.
Warm the fresh cream and stir the saffron into it.
When the chicken is almost cooked, stir in the saffron cream.
Remove from the heat and serve topped with the fried onions, a few drops of rose water and the almonds.

recipes.title: Methi Tadka Dal
recipes.description: Toor dal pressure-cooked with fenugreek leaves and tomatoes, finished with a garlic and curry leaf tadka.

steps.instructionText: Put the toor dal, water, methi leaves, 3 of the tomatoes (chopped), onion, turmeric powder, green chillies, black peppercorns, butter and ginger in a pressure cooker.
Cook until the dal is soft, about 4 whistles.
Heat the ghee in a pan and add the mustard seeds, jeera, garlic, dried red chillies and curry leaves. Fry until the garlic is golden.
Add the remaining tomato, finely chopped, with salt, chilli powder and ground coriander to taste.
Add the cooked dal and let it simmer, adding water if you like it thinner.
Add a few drops of lemon juice and serve with hot rice.

recipes.title: Puliyodarai
recipes.description: Tamil tamarind rice tossed with a roasted spice powder, peanuts and a sesame oil tempering.

steps.instructionText: For the spice powder, dry roast 1 tbsp of the chana dal with the coriander seeds, fenugreek seeds and 3 of the dried red chillies in a pan without oil until deep brown.
Let the mixture cool, then grind it to a fine powder.
Heat the sesame oil in a pan. Add the peanuts and the remaining chana dal and fry until golden brown.
Add the mustard seeds, hing and the remaining red chillies, broken into pieces. When the mustard seeds splutter, take the pan off the stove.
Add the cooked rice, salt, turmeric powder and tamarind concentrate and mix well.
Add the spice powder and curry leaves, mix well and serve.

recipes.title: Puri (Poori)
recipes.description: Small, puffed deep-fried breads made from wheat flour, maida and fine semolina.

steps.instructionText: Put the whole-wheat flour, maida and semolina into a bowl. Add the salt, drizzle over the vegetable oil and mix well.
Gradually mix in enough water to make a stiff dough. Knead it well for a few minutes.
Cover the dough and leave it to rest for about half an hour.
Heat the oil for deep frying in a kadai or other deep pan.
Divide the dough into 8 small balls and roll each into a 7.5 cm circle, using a little hot oil to stop it sticking.
Test the oil with a tiny piece of dough: it should rise to the surface at once.
Lay a puri on the oil and press it gently with a slotted spoon until it puffs up, then turn it over. Adjust the flame as needed.
Fry until golden brown, then drain on a wire rack or kitchen paper.

recipes.title: Puttu (Steamed Rice Cake)
recipes.description: Kerala breakfast of moist rice flour steamed in layers with fresh grated coconut.

steps.instructionText: Grate the coconut finely.
Mix the puttu powder and salt in a wide bowl and add half of the grated coconut.
Rub the mixture with your fingertips, sprinkling in water, until it is moist and has a coarse texture.
If the flour is ready-made, leave the mixture for an hour, as it absorbs more water.
Check the texture: a ball pressed in your hand should crumble easily. Adjust the water if needed.
Spread a little coconut over the bottom of the puttu maker, fill it with the moist flour, and layer it with more coconut.
Steam on the puttu vessel or a pressure cooker nozzle. Once steam escapes from the top, steam for 4 minutes more.
Serve hot with kadala curry, steamed bananas, or boiled green gram and pappad.

recipes.title: Rice Modak
recipes.description: Steamed rice flour dumplings filled with jaggery, coconut, raisins and cashews, a Ganesh Chaturthi favourite.

steps.instructionText: For the filling, melt the jaggery with 4 tbsp water in a pan. Add the coconut and cook, stirring, for 15-20 minutes until thick and almost dry.
Mix in the raisins, cashew nuts and cardamom powder, then spread the filling on a plate to cool.
Heat 2 cups of the water in a large pot and add a pinch of salt and the butter.
When the water boils, add the rice flour, lower the heat and mix to a smooth paste with no lumps. Add the remaining 1/2 cup water if it gets too dry.
Keep stirring on low heat until the rice flour is cooked. Cover with a lid, take off the heat and let it cook in its own steam.
While the dough is still warm, rub ghee on your palms, roll a small portion into a ball and press it into a cup with your thumb.
Put 2 tsp of the filling inside and gather the edges to close it into the shape of a fig.
Make 10 modaks and place them in a steamer basket greased with ghee so that they do not touch.
Steam the modaks for 10 minutes.
Drizzle with a teaspoon of ghee and serve hot.

recipes.title: Vangi Bath (Brinjal Rice)
recipes.description: Rice tossed with fried brinjal, a roasted coriander-coconut spice powder and tangy lemon.

steps.instructionText: Toss the brinjal with 1 tsp of the salt and leave it for half an hour. Rinse lightly and drain.
Heat 1 tbsp of the vegetable oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the coriander seeds, chana dal, cayenne pepper and cinnamon and stir until the spices darken. Remove to a paper towel.
In the same pan, fry the coconut, stirring constantly, until golden brown. Remove to the paper towel.
In another pan, sauté the brinjal in a little oil until cooked through and dark brown. Set aside and keep warm.
Grind the fried spices to a fine powder and mix with the coconut.
In a small pot, bring the lemon juice, 1/2 tsp salt, turmeric and 2 tbsp water to the boil. Lower the heat and simmer for 3 minutes.
Sauté the cooked rice and brinjal in a pan with very little oil, mix well and let cool.
Mix in 2 tbsp of the vegetable oil, the coconut-spice mixture, the lemon mixture and the remaining salt. Serve at room temperature.

recipes.title: Rosogulla (Rasgulla)
recipes.description: Soft, spongy balls of fresh chenna cooked in sugar syrup and served chilled.

steps.instructionText: Dissolve the citric acid in 1/2 cup water and set aside.
Bring the full-cream milk to a boil, stirring. Take it off the heat and keep stirring for 5-7 minutes until slightly cool.
Add the citric acid solution and stir gently until it curdles and the whey is clear. Leave for 3-4 minutes.
Strain through a damp muslin cloth and squeeze lightly 3-4 times to drain most of the whey. Knead the chenna gently until free of lumps; use it straight away.
For the syrup, heat the sugar, the milk for the syrup and 3 cups water in a wide pan, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Bring to a boil and boil for 5 minutes without stirring, so the grey scum collects on top.
Drizzle 1 cup water down the sides of the pan and simmer for 10 minutes, then lift off the grey scum with a slotted spoon.
Boil again, drizzle in another cup of water and skim off the remaining scum. Boil hard for 1-2 minutes and set aside.
Divide the chenna into 16 parts and roll into smooth, crack-free balls. Place them on a plate dusted with a little maida.
Mix 2 tsp maida with 3/4 cup water. Bring the syrup to a vigorous boil in a deep pan and sprinkle in half of this flour solution.
Slide in the chenna balls without touching them. Cook for about 15 minutes, adding the rest of the flour solution when the froth subsides and sprinkling water to keep it frothy.
They are done when they spring back when pressed. Transfer to a bowl with 2 ladles of syrup and 1 cup water, cool, and chill for 3-4 hours.

recipes.title: Sheermal (Saffron Flatbread)
recipes.description: Rich, slightly sweet flatbread made with milk and ghee, splashed with saffron milk as it bakes.

steps.instructionText: Soak the saffron in the warm milk and set aside.
Sift the maida and salt together, then sprinkle in the sugar.
Add the melted ghee and rub it in with your fingers until evenly mixed.
Add the milk a little at a time and knead to a soft, smooth dough. Cover with a damp cloth and rest for 2 hours.
Knead again and rest for another 2 hours.
Knead once more and divide the dough into 7 parts. Rub the saffron into the warm milk to dissolve it.
Place an upturned heavy iron pan on the lower shelf of the oven, set the grill on the upper rack and preheat to 250 °C (480 °F).
On a floured surface, roll each piece into a thick 15 cm round and prick all over with a fork.
Slap the dough onto the hot pan base and bake until brown spots appear.
Move it to the grill with tongs, splash it with the warm saffron milk using your fingertips and bake a few seconds more.
Serve hot, or wrap in a slightly damp towel. Brush with ghee if you like.

recipes.title: Tamate ka Kut
recipes.description: Hyderabadi tomato and gram flour curry tempered with cumin and curry leaves, simmered with boiled eggs.

steps.instructionText: Put the tomatoes in a large non-stick pan with 1 cup water. Cover and cook on medium-low heat until mushy, stirring now and then. Let cool.
Blend the tomatoes with the besan until smooth.
Strain through a wire mesh strainer back into the pan, discarding the seeds and skins. Add 2 cups water and let it simmer.
Heat the oil in a small pan and add the cumin seeds, dried red chillies, garlic and curry leaves. When they splutter, pour them into the tomato sauce.
Add the roasted cumin powder, roasted coriander powder, red chilli powder and salt. Mix well and bring to a boil.
Make light slits on all four sides of the eggs, just through the surface, and add them to the sauce.
Simmer on medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, until the raw smell of besan is gone, about 30 minutes.
Stir in the coriander leaves and mint leaves just before serving, and serve warm.

recipes.title: Keema and Chickpea Pulao
recipes.description: One-pot basmati rice cooked with caramelised onions, spiced lamb mince and chickpeas.

steps.instructionText: Wash the basmati rice in several changes of water and leave it to soak while you prepare the rest.
Heat the oil or ghee in a saucepan and fry the onion over very low heat, stirring often, until it begins to brown, about 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, crush the garlic with a little salt, dice the tomato and drain the chickpeas.
Add the garlic, ground cumin, ground coriander and garam masala to the onion and fry until the onion is deep brown.
Add the tomato and stir briefly. Turn up the heat, add the lamb mince and cook until completely browned, 5-10 minutes.
Drain the rice and add it to the pan with a little extra oil if needed. Stir gently until coated, without breaking the grains.
Add the hot water, chickpeas and salt, and bring to the boil.
Cover with a tight-fitting lid, turn the heat to very low and cook for 25 minutes without lifting the lid.
Add the peas, cover again, turn off the heat and leave to rest for 5 minutes.
Turn out onto a platter, breaking up lumps with the back of a spoon, and serve with yoghurt.

recipes.title: Upeseru (Lentils with Greens)
recipes.description: Karnataka-style lentils and greens with a peppery garlic broth, traditionally eaten with ragi mudde.

steps.instructionText: Fry the mustard seeds, curry leaves, onion and 2 of the green chillies, split lengthwise, in the oil until the onion is partly browned.
Meanwhile, heat the cooked dal, add the spinach and boil until the spinach is tender.
Drain, keeping the cooking water aside for the broth.
Stir the fried spice mixture and salt into the dal and greens and keep on the heat until the flavours blend.
For the broth, lightly dry-roast the remaining green chillies and the tamarind, if you like.
Grind the chillies, tamarind, coriander leaves, garlic, black peppercorns and cumin seeds with a little water to a chutney.
Bring the reserved dal and spinach water to a boil and simmer for 2 minutes.
When serving, stir a spoonful of the chutney into the broth and squeeze in the lemon juice.
Serve the dal and greens with the broth and mudde (ragi balls).

recipes.title: Bhuna Khichuri
recipes.description: Bengali rice and roasted lentils cooked with whole spices and ghee, topped with fried onions.

steps.instructionText: Rinse the basmati rice, moong dal and chana dal separately in cold water. Drain the rice and spread it out to dry.
Soak the moong dal and chana dal in water for 30 minutes.
Drain the dals and dry-roast them briefly until aromatic, then let them cool. Heat the water and keep it hot but not boiling.
Lightly crush the cardamom pods, cloves and cinnamon sticks.
Heat 2 tbsp of the ghee in a heavy pan over medium heat. Add the bay leaves and crushed spices; when they sputter, add the ginger and cumin seeds and stir for 1-2 minutes.
Add the green chillies and green peas and stir once or twice.
Add the rice and stir gently for 2-3 minutes until it is well coated.
Add the dals, turmeric powder and salt and stir for 1-2 minutes more.
Pour in hot water to about 2.5 cm above the mixture. Lower the heat, cover and simmer for about 10 minutes until the rice is firm and separate, checking it does not stick.
Meanwhile, fry the onion in the remaining ghee over medium heat until it starts to brown.
Top the khichuri with the fried onion and its ghee, garnish with the coriander leaves, then cover and keep on the lowest heat until serving.

recipes.title: Bangladeshi Chicken Curry
recipes.description: Chicken stewed in a tomato, onion and ginger sauce, finished with yogurt and fresh lime juice.

steps.instructionText: Nick the skin of each tomato and cover with very hot water for 20 seconds, then drain. Peel, halve, squeeze out the seeds and roughly chop the flesh.
Finely chop the onion and fry it in the vegetable oil in a heavy pan over low-medium heat for about 10 minutes, stirring, until evenly golden.
Meanwhile, finely chop the ginger and garlic. Slit the green chillies, remove the seeds (keep some for more heat) and chop finely.
Add the ginger, garlic and green chillies to the pan and fry for about a minute.
Add the ground coriander, ground cumin and ground turmeric and fry for 1-2 minutes, stirring. Season with salt and black pepper.
Add the water and tomatoes, bring to the boil, then lower the heat and simmer for 5-10 minutes.
Add the chicken and stir to coat it with the sauce. Cover and cook on low heat for 30-40 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the yogurt. When the sauce bubbles again, taste it and squeeze in the juice of half the lime, adding the rest if needed.
Sprinkle with chopped coriander leaves and serve with the cooked rice.

recipes.title: Sindhi Besan Kadhi
recipes.description: Simple Sindhi curry of roasted besan and tomatoes, tempered with cumin, mustard seeds and curry leaves.

steps.instructionText: Heat the oil in a pan and add the cumin and mustard seeds, curry leaves and green chillies. Fry for a few minutes.
Stir in the besan and cook, stirring, until it turns golden.
Mix in the water and keep stirring for at least 5 minutes.
Add the coriander leaves, tomatoes, salt, red chilli powder and turmeric, and simmer until thick.
Serve hot with white rice and fried potatoes.

recipes.title: Steamed Baingan Bharta
recipes.description: Steamed, mashed aubergine cooked with onion, ginger, garlic and tomato, with an optional charcoal smoke.

ingredients.name: tomato paste (or 4 ripe tomatoes, finely diced)
coriander, stems and leaves chopped separately

steps.instructionText: Peel and steam the baingan until the flesh is tender, then mash it.
Heat the mustard oil in a pan.
Add the mustard seeds and cumin seeds and sauté for 10 seconds.
Add the garlic and ginger and sauté until they turn yellow.
Add the onion and sauté until translucent.
Add the mashed baingan, turmeric powder, coriander stems, tomato paste, green chillies and salt. Cook on medium heat for 20 minutes.
For a smoky flavour, set a small piece of lit charcoal on foil in the dish, pour 1/4 tsp mustard oil over it and cover at once to infuse.
Garnish with the coriander leaves and serve.

recipes.title: Arisa Pitha
recipes.description: Odia festive sweet of jaggery rice dough stuffed with coconut and sesame, then deep fried until crisp.

ingredients.name: ghee, plus extra for the filling
vegetable oil or ghee, for deep frying

steps.instructionText: Boil the water in a wide pan. Stir in the jaggery, salt, cinnamon powder and 1 tbsp ghee.
Slowly add the rice flour, stirring continuously. Cover and cook on low heat until the water is absorbed and the dough is like chapati dough. Let it cool.
For the filling, melt a little ghee in a pan over medium heat. Add the coconut and sugar and cook, stirring, until the coconut turns golden brown.
Knead the cooled rice mixture into a smooth dough.
Make small balls of dough, flatten them, and stuff each with some of the coconut filling and a few sesame seeds.
Deep fry the filled pithas in the vegetable oil or ghee until golden brown all over.

recipes.title: Avakaya (Mango Pickle)
recipes.description: Fiery Andhra raw mango pickle with mustard, chilli, fenugreek and garlic in sesame oil.

steps.instructionText: Soak the mangoes in water for 10 minutes, then dry them with a clean cloth.
Cut each mango in half vertically so the hard stone is also cut in two, each half staying firmly attached. Remove the kernel and scrape off its thin skin.
Cut each half into 4-5 pieces, each with a bit of stone so it stays firm. Wipe the pieces with a dry cloth and put them in a large basin.
Sprinkle the turmeric powder over the mango pieces and mix with dry hands.
Pour half of the sesame oil over the pieces and mix well by hand; coating them in oil first keeps them firm.
Mix the powdered salt into the mango.
In another bowl, mix the mustard powder, red chilli powder, garlic paste and fenugreek seed powder with half of the remaining sesame oil to a paste you can hold in a fist.
Mix the paste well into the mango pieces, then mix in the rest of the sesame oil.
Cover tightly with a lid, or move to a porcelain jar or clean container with a firm lid. Tie a thick cloth over it and store on a cool, dark shelf.
After 3-4 days, open, mix well and taste. Add a little salt or red chilli powder if needed, and stir in the garlic flakes.
Transfer the pickle to clean glass or porcelain jars.
